sections.h2: How can a Clay homeowner sell, and which route fits?
sections.html:
Three routes are open to a Clay owner: an agent listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. Which one wins depends on the calendar, the condition of the roof and mechanicals, and whether you can keep paying the mortgage and the January tax bill while a house sits on the market.

A listing exposes the house to the most buyers, yet it means cleaning, staging, weekend showings and a buyer whose lender may balk at an appraisal. A cash purchase trims that list to a walkthrough and a closing date. Expect a cash number to land under a polished listing price, so line the two up on what you would actually keep after payoff, taxes and fees.

  • An agent suits a tidy house and an owner with months to spare.
  • A sale without an agent suits someone who already knows the buyer, such as a neighbor or relative.
  • A cash buyer suits a rental with tenants, an inherited house, a property that needs work or a move with a hard deadline.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the town of Clay itself?
sections.html:
Clay is the largest town in Onondaga County, set just north of Syracuse. The Oneida River forms the northern boundary with Oswego County, and the Seneca River runs along the western edge. Retail clusters along NY Route 31, and NY Route 481 meets it near Euclid. The town was carved from Cicero in 1827 and carries the name of Henry Clay.

Buyers see two kinds of housing. Planned subdivisions such as Fairway East, Lawton Valley Hunt, Country Meadow and The Farmstead sit next to older hamlets including Euclid, Moyers Corners, Belgium and Three Rivers. Micron Technology announced a chip complex at the White Pine Commerce Park in Clay in October 2022, a project that keeps the town in regional headlines.

Most of the housing stock dates from a postwar surge. The population rose from 7,001 in 1950 to 17,760 in 1960 and 36,274 in 1970, then reached 52,838 by 1980. Houses built in that stretch are now fifty to seventy years old, which is why roofs, windows and heating systems come up in so many Clay sales. Mailing addresses vary by corner of town: ZIP codes include 13041 for Clay, 13090 for Bayberry, 13212 for North Syracuse, 13088 for Liverpool and 13029 for Brewerton.

Census counted 60,527 people in 2020 and estimates 59,285 for July 1, 2025. These housing and income figures frame a pricing conversation.

sections.h2: Which Clay school districts and tax lines show up on a bill?
sections.html:
Five school districts reach into the town. The Tax Receiver names Liverpool and North Syracuse as the two largest, with smaller pieces belonging to Baldwinsville, Phoenix and Central Square. The district printed on a bill often steers how buyers think about a house.

It also steers the cost. The assessor's tax page shows school rates per thousand dollars of full market value running from $18.58 in Central Square to $28.21 in Liverpool, with North Syracuse at $23.22. The county rate is listed at $5.14. Town levies add $1.94 for highways, $0.96 for fire protection and $0.75 for administration, and a county sewer charge of $417.07 is listed for each residential unit. Ask the assessor which tax year those numbers describe before quoting them.

Five volunteer fire departments protect the town under contract, and the Town runs one water district. Buyers read every line, so have a recent bill ready.

sections.h2: What does the Clay tax calendar mean for a seller?
sections.html:
Most parcels get two bills a year: Town and County in January and school in the fall. Houses in the Village of North Syracuse get a third, a village bill in early summer. The Tax Receiver collects all of them.

  • Town and County: mailed around January 1, due without penalty January 31.
  • School: mailed around September 1, due without penalty around October 1.
  • North Syracuse village: mailed around June 1, due without penalty July 1.
  • Water: the Tax Office also takes payments for the Town's single water district.

Because parcels sit in different districts, the September bill can differ sharply between two similar houses on neighboring streets. If your house is inside the Village of North Syracuse, the summer village bill is an extra one that owners outside the village never see.

You can pay through the Onondaga County Department of Finance website, mail a check, or use the secured drop box outside Town Hall at 4401 State Route 31. The title company will split these bills between you and the buyer on the closing statement. Get a current payoff figure from the Tax Receiver before closing instead of leaning on last year's paper.

sections.h2: How do Clay assessments and grievances work?
sections.html:
State law sets the assessor's year. March 1 is the taxable status date and also the last day to file any exemption, with no exceptions. May 1 brings the tentative roll, the fourth Tuesday in May is Grievance Day, and July 1 makes the roll final.

This year's hearing took place May 26, 2026, from 4 to 8 p.m. at Town Hall, and it is over. Next spring's falls on the fourth Tuesday of May 2027. Once it passes, values stay put until the next taxable status year, and they drive both the September school bill and the January Town and County bill. A grievance form and filing instructions are posted on the Town site.

A grievance will not rescue a sale already in motion, but the roll still tells a buyer's lender the taxable value. The assessor handles veterans, senior, disability and limited-income, agricultural, clergy, nonprofit and commercial or industrial exemptions. Basic STAR is registered through New York State rather than the Town.

sections.h2: Who handles permits, deeds and utilities for a Clay sale?
sections.html:
The Town's department directory lists the assessor, code enforcement, planning and development, highway, the Tax Receiver, the Town Clerk and water. Code enforcement covers building permits, inspections and zoning compliance, so it is the office to ask about a finished basement or a deck that went up without paperwork.

The Onondaga County Clerk, not the Town, files deeds. New York charges transfer tax of $2 per $500 of consideration, normally on the seller, and Form TP-584 goes to the clerk with the deed no later than 15 days after delivery. Ask the clerk for current recording charges. The Town Clerk keeps local records. Before closing, make sure open permits are closed and that no unpaid water or sewer balance sits on the parcel.

faqs.q: Does a Clay house with deferred repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes, though the price follows the work. A buyer who takes the house as-is expects a discount for the roof, furnace or siding. Ask code enforcement about open permits first, because those can delay any closing.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a Clay house?
faqs.a: The Clay Tax Receiver bills Town, County, school and North Syracuse village taxes for parcels inside the Town. Town and County payments are due January 31 and school payments around October 1.

faqs.q: Can I still file a grievance for Clay this year?
faqs.a: No. The 2026 hearing was May 26. Plan for the fourth Tuesday of May 2027, and file any exemption application by March 1 of that year.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Clay address?
faqs.a: It varies by parcel across Liverpool, North Syracuse, Baldwinsville, Phoenix and Central Square. The school bill names the district, and the Tax Receiver can confirm it.

faqs.q: Where does a Clay deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Onondaga County Clerk. Call that office for current forms and fees before you set a closing date.
